section5_rewrite_outline: 5.1 Panorama overview (7-asset setup, PIT protocol, K-experiment progression)
5.2 Results by asset class (Table 5.1 panorama DM t + Table 5.2 QLIKE)
5.3 TLT finstress outlier as lag-sensitive regime artefact (three-piece evidence)
5.5 Final narrative commitment on native-IV sufficiency across 7 assets
5.6 Limitations and future work (asset coverage / PIT database / ^VXEEM / TLT rates-native follow-up / daily HAR-RV)
final_narrative_commitment_quote: Native implied-volatility proxies (^VIX, ^VXN, ^OVX, ^GVZ, ^MOVE, and ^VXEEM-or-proxy with rv30 robustness) are sufficient for one-step-ahead realised-volatility forecasting across seven asset classes (SPY, QQQ, GLD, USO, TLT, BTC-USD, EEM). Alt-data (EPU / WLEMU / NFCI / ANFCI / STLFSI) cannot deliver Harvey (2016) |t|>3 improvement over the native-IV baseline under point-in-time publication-lag alignment. The only cell exceeding the threshold (TLT / finstress, DM t = +3.74 at pit_shift0) fails the 5% QLIKE economic gate (+0.50%), the pit_shift1 robustness check (+2.00, Harvey-insignificant), and the kitchen-sink 'all' spec (-5.67), and is therefore characterised as a non-structural regime artefact rather than a replicable rates-specific signal.
